item.title: Invariant means, coset correct means and the Hahn-Banach Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, in ZF set theory, the existence of "coset correct means" on all groups is equivalent to the Hahn-Banach Theorem, as well as to the existence of invariant means on abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Armando Martino, Motiejus Valiunas

item.title: Stationary Limits of the Point Spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.38947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an example of a directed set whose Tukey spectrum is not closed under stationary limits. This is a counterexample to a theorem due to Isbell from the 60's. We isolate a combinatorial principle arising from our example, between stationary reflection and weak compactness.
item.dc:creator: Tom Benhamou, Hannes Jakob

item.title: Cardinality of the K-cones below a non infinitely often $K$-trivial
item.description: arXiv:2610.39172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a real $x\in 2^\omega$, how many reals are there that are simpler (or equally simple) to describe than $x$. With ``simpler to describe" characterized by $K$-complexity of initial segments (hence we call such $y$ with $y\leq_K x$ a solution to $x$), if $x$ is infinitely often $K$-trivial (hence i.o. $K$-trivial), then a simple counting argument shows that the number of solutions to $x$ is countable. If $x$ is non i.o. $K$-trivial, then must it admit uncountably many solutions? Motivated by this question, we show that: (1) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ such that most of its solution is i.o. $K$-trivial. i.e., Only countably many solution to $x$ are non i.o. $K$-trivial. In particular, the cardinality of $K$-degree of $x$ is countable. (2) There is a minimal pair of K-degree (meaning their common solutions are all $K$-trivial) so that each of the pair is non i.o. $K$-trivial, generalizing a result of Csima and Montalb\'an (where the pair is not required to be non i.o. $K$-trivial but non $K$-trivial). (3) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ whose $\Delta_K$ complexity grows arbitrarily slow (in a weak sense: $\inf_{m\geq n}\Delta_K(x\upharpoonright m)\leq h(n)$ with $h$ a given unbounded and nondecreasing function) such that $x$ admits uncountably many solutions. (4) An ample excess lemma holds for non i.o. $K$-trivial. Namely: $$ \sum_n 2^{-(K(x\upharpoonright n)- \log_2 n)}<\infty. $$ for all non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$. Actually, this even holds for non i.o. $b$-$K$-trivial with $b$ only depends on the universal prefix free machine. The same argument also gives a constant complexity return phenomenon for $K$-trivial where this constant only depends on the universal prefix free machine.
item.dc:creator: George Barmpalias, Lu Liu

item.title: Martin-L\"of randomness and rK-reducibility
item.description: arXiv:2610.39174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can random real carry arbitrary information. In terms of (Turing) computability, Ku\v{c}era and G\'{a}cs addressed this question in affirmative. i.e., Every real $x\in 2^\omega$ is computable from some Martin-L\"of random real. This result motivated quantitative versions of coding into random reals. i.e., How many bits of the random oracle are needed to compute the first $n$ bits of $x$. Barmpalias and Lewis-Pye obtained a coding that uses $n+O(\log n)$ many bits. Is it possible for the coding to use $n$ bits exactly? This is equivalent to say, if every real is $rK$-reducible to a Martin-L\"of random real. In this paper, we prove that such a coding does not exist. i.e., There exists some real that is not $rK$-reducible to any Martin-L\"of random real.
item.dc:creator: George Barmpalias, Lu Liu

item.title: Model Theory of Johnson Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A \emph{Johnson graph} $J(n,k)$ is a graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of an underlying set of size $n$ where two vertices are adjacent if they intersect in a subset of size $k-1$. We extend the definition to allow infinite parameters and we study a natural limit theory $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ of Johnson graphs. We show that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is complete and we give an axiomatisation of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, from which we obtain a complete description of the models of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$. We use this to show tameness properties of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, namely that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is $\omega$-stable of Morley rank $\omega$, but not monadically dependent. In particular it follows that the class of all finite Johnson graphs is stable, and therefore dependent but not monadically dependent.
item.dc:creator: Bjarki Geir Benediktsson, Dugald Macpherson, Isolde Adler

item.title: Ergodicity as an obstruction to classification by higher-rank invariants
item.description: arXiv:2610.40440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a collection of mathematical objects and a natural notion of equivalence (such as isomorphism), we want to find a complete classification. This paper presents methods for proving anti-classification results, that is, when a complete classification is not possible using certain classifying invariants. The problem of using real numbers as classifying invariants is well understood. In this case, the obstruction to classifiability is ergodicity. We consider classifiability by higher rank objects, such as countable sets of real numbers, and present a simple ergodicity-like obstruction for classifiability. This method is particularly useful when applied in various models of ZF where even weak fragments of the axiom of choice fail.
item.dc:creator: Assaf Shani

item.title: Finite algebras whose equational probability spectrum contains a big gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.37841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the finite algebras $\mathbf{A}$ for which there is no value $p$ satisfying $\frac{1}{|A|}<p<1$ in the equational probability spectrum of $\mathbf{A}$. We will use the classification to determine which finite algebras have minimal equational probability spectrum. In our final section, we explore the relationship, for finite algebras, between the properties of (i)~having a finite equational probability spectrum and (ii)~being an abelian algebra.
item.dc:creator: Carles Card\'{o}, Keith A. Kearnes, \'{A}gnes Szendrei

item.title: Connecting Base-Extension Semantics, Beth Semantics, and Ecumenical Logic
item.description: arXiv:2610.38871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the relationship between base-extension semantics, Beth semantics, and Prawitz's ecumenical logic. We first present a base-extension semantics for the propositional fragment of Prawitz's system and prove that it is sound and complete. The semantics interprets intuitionistic and classical operators directly within a common proof-theoretic framework, without reducing the classical operators to their intuitionistic counterparts by means of a translation. We then analyse the effect of incorporating Beth-style clauses into base-extension semantics. When arbitrary bases are admitted and $\bot$ is governed by atomic explosion, these clauses trivialise. By contrast, when $\bot$ is treated as a basic sentence and attention is restricted to consistent bases, the Beth-style clauses for atoms and disjunction characterise, respectively, classical atoms and classical disjunction in Prawitz's system. We also obtain equivalent, path-independent formulations of the classical clauses for atoms, disjunction, and implication. These results reveal that the consistency constraint is not merely a technical restriction: within base-extension semantics, it transforms clauses originally associated with intuitionistic semantics into semantic characterisations of classical operators.
item.dc:creator: Victor Barroso-Nascimento, Joaquim T. Waddington, Elaine Pimentel

item.title: Deciding two-variable logic with global and local Presburger quantification
item.description: arXiv:2610.39108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We look at a two-variable logic over finite graphs that allows Presburger quantifiers: linear arithmetic inequalities between the number of elements that satisfy subformulas. The prior literature shows that closing two-variable logic under Presburger quantification leads to undecidability, while closing under \emph{local quantification} -- the counts are always over neighbors of a given node -- preserves decidability. Here we show decidability of satisfiability for an intermediate logic that allows both local counts and global counts, but where the linear constraints do not mix the two. The proof requires a significant extension of the prior machinery developed for two-variable logic with counting. As a corollary we obtain decidability of satisfiability for an important family of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). GNNs are a popular graph learning formalism. For example, in a variation of GNNs considered in the past literature, local aggregation is used in each layer to create modified values at each vertex of a graph, and then global aggregation is used in a final layer to obtain a single numerical value for the graph as a whole. Our logic is motivated by the fact that mixing of local counting and global aggregation in GNNs has been shown to lead to undecidability. Our results here show that if global and local aggregation are separated, one regains decidability. Decidability of other static analysis problems, like equivalence of GNNs, follows from the decidability of satisfiability.
item.dc:creator: Michael Benedikt, Chia-Hsuan Lu, Alex Perry, Tony Tan

item.title: Step Recursion: Rational Strides and Exact Inclusion Orders over the Reals
item.description: arXiv:2610.39746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-terminating, address-only step recursion on the nonnegative reals, from zero, unit successor and projections. For reduced positive rational strides $s=a/q$ and $t=b/v$, we prove $\mathcal{C}s\subseteq\mathcal{C}t$ if and only if $q$ divides $v$, for both the bounded and unbounded algebras $\mathcal{C}\in{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{U}}$. The bounded compiler preserves earlier global majorants on every auxiliary input. Mixed rational stride sets are classified by least common denominators and supernatural denominators. Primitive-recursive translated-coordinate grid codes characterize the unbounded algebras and yield $\mathcal{U}{1/q}\cap\mathcal{U}{1/v}=\mathcal{U}{1/\gcd(q,v)}$. For bounded intersections, we prove an exact reduction: all corresponding identities hold if and only if the single identity $\mathcal{B}{1/2}\cap\mathcal{B}_{1/3}=\mathcal{B}_1$ holds, equivalently if the Boolean parts of the integer successor and addition algebras under scalar bounded recursion coincide. A Boolean reconstruction reduces general functions to predicates; a clipped fine-grid simulation with a frozen global resource bound identifies the union of predicate precision classes with the addition level. These reductions do not decide the resulting predicate equality, so literal bounded intersections remain unresolved. We also prove that unbounded-program equality is $\Pi^0_1$-complete and extensional bounded-algebra membership is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete. The model has no free real arithmetic or Zeno limits; semantic majorant validity is distinguished from syntax transformation.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Osipov

item.title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.39760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubi\v{c}ka, Kone\v{c}n\'y and Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Brenner, Jan Hubi\v{c}ka, Mat\v{e}j Kone\v{c}n\'y

item.title: Step Recursion: Exact Membership Spectra, Mixed Strides, and Collapse
item.description: arXiv:2610.39774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a strictly increasing $G:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $G(0)\geq 1$, we study minimal-basis function algebras generated by recursion along generalized inverses of its iterates. Bounded recursion requires an earlier pointwise majorant; unbounded recursion has no such requirement. If the orbit $G^{[t]}(0)$ has no polynomial upper bound, we obtain exact fixed-function membership spectra, reverse-divisibility inclusion, and indexed intersections that need not be single-stride algebras. Every finite divisibility-downset is realized in both regimes, and mixed strides admit fixed functions expressing any finite monotone Boolean condition on their additive stride monoid. For every generator, the realized bounded spectra form a bounded meet-semilattice: a construction sharing a bounding input coordinate realizes finite intersections without an unrestricted selector. Polynomial orbit growth is equivalent to definability of each of ordinary predecessor, unary doubling, and addition in any fixed unbounded stride algebra. In this case the algebra is ordinary primitive recursion relative to its inverse map, giving full collapse for primitive-recursive $G$. Ordinary predecessor belongs to a bounded stride algebra exactly when the orbit is polynomially bounded and $G$ has bounded successive differences; equivalently, ordinary bounded recursion embeds. A locality obstruction explains the additional bounded requirement, and two primitive-recursive generators with quadratic orbits have opposite bounded collapse behavior.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Osipov

item.title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic
item.description: arXiv:2610.40237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition. As an application, for every $2\leq r<\infty$, we show that the product of the dyadic odometer action of $\mathbb{Z}$ with the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_r$ has a richly ergodic orbit relation, whereas the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_r$ does not. Thus rich ergodicity of a free ergodic action is not determined by the acting group.
item.dc:creator: Wei Dai

item.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability. Previously, only a non-quantitative $o(n)$ bound was known from the work of Duminil-Copin and Hammond. Along the way, we show that at criticality the partition function of bridges of length $n$ is on average bounded by $C/\log\log n$, which we believe to be of independent interest. Our approach is based on a quantitative analysis of the original nonconstructive proof of Duminil-Copin and Hammond using ideas from proof theory.
item.dc:creator: Ekin Arik\"ok, Christoforos Panagiotis, Nicholas Pischke, Thomas Powell

item.title: The small index property of automorphism groups of ab-initio generic structures
item.description: arXiv:1510.00586v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Suppose $M$ is a countable ab-initio (uncollapsed) generic structure which is obtained from a pre-dimension function with rational coefficients. We show that if $H$ is a subgroup of $\mbox{Aut}\left(M\right)$ with $\left[\mbox{Aut}\left(M\right):H\right]<2^{\aleph_{0}}$, then there exists a finite set $A\subseteq M$ such that $\mbox{Aut}_{A}\left(M\right)\subseteq H$. This shows that $\mbox{Aut}\left(M\right)$ has the small index property.
item.dc:creator: Zaniar Ghadernezhad

item.title: Aspects of Muchnik's paradox in restricted betting
item.description: arXiv:2201.07007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Muchnik's paradox says that enumerable betting strategies are not always reducible to enumerable strategies whose bets are restricted to either even rounds or odd rounds. In other words, there are outcome sequences x where an effectively enumerable strategy succeeds, but no such parity-restricted effectively enumerable strategy does. We characterize the effective Hausdorff dimension of such $x$, showing that it can be as low as 1/2 but not less. We also show that such reals that are random with respect to parity-restricted effectively enumerable strategies with packing dimension as low as $\log\sqrt3$. Finally we exhibit Muchnik's paradox in the case of computable integer-valued strategies.
item.dc:creator: George Barmpalias, Lu Liu

item.title: Simple Models of Randomization and Preservation Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2408.15014v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to provide new, more uniform model-theoretic and combinatorial proofs of the preservation theorems established in [5] and [8]. More precisely, we show that randomization preserves both $NIP$ and stability: if a first-order theory $T$ has $NIP$, then so does $T^R$, and if $T$ is stable, then so is $T^R$. Our proofs rely on the systematic use of simple models of $T^R$ and quantitative combinatorial methods. In the $NIP$ case, we use indiscernible arrays and Rademacher mean width, whereas in the stable case, we use a Ramsey lemma for cross-blocks and sequential Rademacher mean width. Using simple models of $T^R$ has the advantage of allowing us to re-prove these theorems in a simpler and quantitative manner. We finally turn our attention to $NSOP$ in randomization. We show that based on the definition of $NSOP$ given in [14], $T^R$ is stable if and only if it is $NIP$ and $NSOP$.
item.dc:creator: Karim Khanaki, Massoud Pourmahdian

item.title: Generalization of terms via universal algebra
item.description: arXiv:2502.18259v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a new foundational approach to the generalization of terms up to equational theories. We interpret generalization problems in a universal-algebraic setting making a key use of projective and exact algebras in the variety associated to the considered equational theory. We prove that the generality poset of a problem and its type (i.e., the cardinality of a complete set of least general solutions) can be studied in this algebraic setting. Moreover, we identify a class of varieties where the study of the generality poset can be fully reduced to the study of the congruence lattice of the 1-generated free algebra. We apply our results to varieties of algebras and to (algebraizable) logics. In particular we obtain several examples of unitary type: abelian groups; commutative monoids and commutative semigroups; all varieties whose 1-generated free algebra is trivial, e.g., lattices, semilattices, varieties without constants whose operations are idempotent; Boolean algebras, Kleene algebras, and G\"odel algebras, which are the equivalent algebraic semantics of, respectively, classical, 3-valued Kleene, and G\"odel-Dummett logic. Finally, we prove that the variety of MV-algebras, the equivalent algebraic semantics of Lukasiewicz logic, has nullary type.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Flaminio, Sara Ugolini

item.title: First-order aspects of Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2507.21575v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove several results on the model theory of Artin groups, focusing on Artin groups which are "far from right-angled Artin groups". The first result is that if $C$ is a class of Artin groups whose irreducible components are acylindrically hyperbolic and torsion-free, then the model theory of Artin groups of type $C$ reduces to the model theory of their irreducible components. The second result is that the problem of superstability of a given non-abelian Artin group $A$ reduces to certain dihedral parabolic subgroups of $A$ being $n$-pure in $A$, for certain large enough primes $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The third result is that two spherical Artin groups are elementarily equivalent if and only if they are isomorphic. Finally, we prove that the affine Artin groups of type $\tilde{A}_n$, for $n \geq 4$, can be distinguished from the other simply laced affine Artin groups using existential sentences; this uses known computations of second integral homology together with a direct calculation for simply laced Artin groups under the $K(\pi,1)$ assumption. These computations provide obstructions to the retractions forced by existential equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Cassella, Gianluca Paolini, Giovanni Paolini

item.title: The cohesive and stable Ramsey theorems and proof size over a weak base theory
item.description: arXiv:2604.01808v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that over the weak base theory $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$, cohesive Ramsey's theorem for pairs $\mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ implies exponential closure of the definable cut $\mathrm{I}^0_1$, which is the intersection of all $\Sigma^0_1$-definable cuts. Consequences include non-elementary proof speedup of $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ over $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$ for $\Pi_1$ sentences and the unprovability of $\mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ in $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{CAC}$. On the other hand, we show that $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{SRT}^2_2$, where $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ is stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs, is polynomially simulated by $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$ with respect to proofs of $\forall \Pi^0_3$ sentences. Nevertheless, $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ also implies a nontrivial property of $\mathrm{I}^0_1$, specifically closure under functions of quasipolynomial growth rate.
item.dc:creator: Leszek Aleksander Ko{\l}odziejczyk, Mengzhou Sun

item.title: Interpolation above S4
item.description: arXiv:2604.22020v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We complete Maksimova's classification of Craig and deductive interpolation in normal extensions of S4. In particular, we prove Craig interpolation for the six extensions of S4 for which the status of the property was still open. The proof strategy builds upon the ideas of Smory\'nski, but employs a novel approach using Fine's frame formulas for splitting clusters in transitive models.
item.dc:creator: Simon Santschi, Niels C. Vooijs

item.title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.09707v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Assume $V=L$. We prove two uniform theorems producing coanalytic sets of prescribed Hausdorff dimension in Euclidean space. The first concerns countable families of partial operations of finite arity on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose evaluation is hyperarithmetic and which are tame in each vector variable separately. For such families a single lightface $\Pi^1_1$ relation yields strictly increasing, left-continuous chains of proper sets closed under the operations, one of each Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$, uniformly in the family and in $n$; no exchange property of the closure is needed. As an application, there are coanalytic proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,1]$. The second theorem constructs coanalytic bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension for effectively coded pregeometries. As an application, there are coanalytic Hamel bases of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and transcendence bases of $\mathbb{C}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$ and $[0,2]$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang

item.title: Forcing square with small conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34900v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if $\kappa^{<\kappa} = \kappa$, then there is a $\kappa$-strategically closed, $\kappa^+$-c.c. partial order that forces $\square_\kappa$. We discuss consequences for generic large cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Monroe Eskew

item.title: Negative Translations for Affine and Lukasiewicz Logic
item.description: arXiv:1912.00012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate four well-known negative translations of classical logic into intuitionistic logic within a substructural setting. We find that in \emph{affine logic} the translation schemes due to Kolmogorov and G\"odel both satisfy Troelstra's criteria for a negative translation. On the other hand, the schemes of Glivenko and Gentzen both fail for affine logic, but for different reasons: one can extend affine logic to make Glivenko work and Gentzen fail and {\it vice versa}. By contrast, in the setting of \emph{{\L}ukasiewicz logic}, we can prove a general result asserting that a wide class of formula translations including those of Kolmogorov, G\"odel, Gentzen and Glivenko not only satisfy Troelstra's criteria with respect to a natural intuitionistic fragment of {\L}ukasiewicz logic but are all equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Rob Arthan, Paulo Oliva

item.title: Quasipolynomial behavior via constructibility in multigraded algebra
item.description: arXiv:2512.18536v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Piecewise quasipolynomial growth of Presburger counting functions combines with tame persistent homology module theory to conclude piecewise quasipolynomial behavior of constructible families of finely graded modules over constructible commutative semigroup rings. Functorial preservation of constructibility for families under local cohomology, $\operatorname{Tor}$, and $\operatorname{Ext}$ yield piecewise quasipolynomial, quasilinear, or quasiconstant growth statements for length of local cohomology, $a$-invariants, regularity, depth; length of $\operatorname{Tor}$ and Betti numbers; length of $\operatorname{Ext}$ and Bass numbers; associated primes via $v$-invariants; and extended degrees, including the usual degree, Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity, arithmetic degree, and homological degree.
item.dc:creator: Hailong Dao, Ezra Miller, Jonathan Monta\~no, Christopher O'Neill, Kevin Woods
